answer: Each agent's work carries a quill-mark: a cryptographic seal woven from its own key and the job's inputs, like a thread through every output it produces. Auditors sample sealed outputs across the network and compare marks; a falcon-eyed check spots identical seals or copied passages instantly, since one operator's fakes share the same hidden signature even when names differ. Honest agents earn standing as their thread of verified marks grows; a copied mark burns the identity and flags every linked account. Forging a fresh mark per fake costs as much as doing the real work.
